ModMetaData.name: RimMCP
ModMetaData.author: rakan
ModMetaData.description:
Agentic intelligence for the Rim.
What is this? RimMCP connects your colony to any AI agent with MCP support. Your agent will be able to see and do almost anything in the game.
For the modern high-impact 10x engineer.
What does it let agents do? • See. Pawns, stockpiles, bills, research, threats, the map itself, even your mod list and error log. • Do. Zones, stockpiles, blueprints, mining, bills, work priorities, policies, research. • Command. Draft, move, attack, rescue, tend, equip. Use their right-click orders and abilities (Mod actions supported) • Time. Control speed, pause, run the game. • Handle. Read alerts and letters, accept quests, choose rewards, answer dialogs. • Prepare agentically Pick the scenario, world, landing site, ideoligion and colonists through the game's setup screens. • Save. Save, load, and return to the main menu. • Talk. Tell you what they're doing, or send a letter when something needs your attention.
Access Presets Full control (default): Do everything, including storyteller, difficulty, saves and new games. Control: Run the colony, including letters and quests, but not change game settings, save, load or set up games. Administration: Read, manage colony settings and run time, but not give direct orders. Read only: Look, but no actions.
Fine-tune access by switching individual tools on or off in mod settings.
Things to try • "Anyone worth trying to recruit from the injured raiders?" • "Make a corn field on the rich soil, queue up meals." • "Figure out the most efficient fabric available, order clothes for the colony and set up apparel policies." • "Which mod is throwing red errors and why?" • "Destroy the Mechhive, make no mistakes." • "Reroll colonists until we have a well-rounded colony and two shooters." • "Keep me posted on anything that needs my attention."
Requirements • RimWorld 1.6 or 1.7. • An AI client with support for local (stdio) MCP servers. Tested with Codex, Claude Code & OpenCode.
Setup 1. Enable RimMCP in your mod list and restart the game. 2. Go to Options > Mod settings > RimMCP and click Copy MCP config. 3. Add that config to your client's MCP settings (or paste it to your agent and tell it to configure itself, who has time to edit tomls nowadays). 4. Turn on RimWorld's Run in background option so requests work while you're alt-tabbed.
Frequently asked Mid-save compatible? Yes. Agent letters stay in your History like any other letter, but nothing in your save needs RimMCP. Feel free to add or remove at will.
Performance? Near 0 impact when idling. When your agent calls tools, most requests are handled in milliseconds. Token wise, full game control and repeatedly reading pawns can consume a lot of tokens, keep an eye on your usage if you're enabling everything. Since 1.2, reading a pawn costs about a third of what it used to.
What is my agent doing? A cursor with its name shows where it acts. The RimMCP button on the bottom bar opens the agent log: everything it did, and what it was refused and why.
Multiplayer Mod? Supported, read-only operations will work, but anything that changes the game or the clock is refused during a Multiplayer session.
Privacy? If your client uses a cloud model, it may send colony data to that provider. Your colony data could help shape the mind of future LLMs, what could possibly go wrong?
Source: https://github.com/rakanssh/rimcp | Bugs: https://github.com/rakanssh/rimcp/issues
